A.label: Reading A
A.title: POWERING THE PLANET

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Despite modern society’s heavy dependence on fossil fuels for energy, most people are aware that the supply of these fuels is finite. As oil and other fossil fuels become more costly and difficult to find, researchers are looking at alternative energy sources, including solar, wind, and even nuclear power. But which substitute—if any—is the right one?

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.heading: Solar
paragraphs.text: Solar panels catch energy directly from the sun and convert it into electricity. One of the world’s largest solar power stations is in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu, where more than 2.5 million solar panels have the capacity to generate enough power for 750,000 people. But unlike the burning of fossil fuels, the process used to create all that solar energy produces no emissions.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Today, however, solar power provides less than 2 percent of the world’s energy, primarily because the cost of the panels is still very high. But price is only one issue. Clouds and darkness also cause solar panels to produce less energy. This requires that additional power sources (such as batteries) be available.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Some scientists think the solution to this problem can be found in space, which is the ideal place to gather energy from the sun. With no clouds and no nighttime, a space-based solar power station could operate constantly. These stations would send the power back to Earth, which could then be turned into electricity for consumption. Advocates of solar space stations say this technology would initially require a lot of money, but eventually it could provide continuous, clean energy that would be cheaper than other fuels. Also, unlike other energy sources, solar power from space would last as long as the sun shines, and would guarantee everyone on Earth all the energy they need.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.heading: Wind
paragraphs.text: Wind—the fastest-growing alternative energy source—is another way of collecting energy from the sun. Wind is caused by the sun’s heat rather than its light. Therefore, unlike solar power, wind power works well even on cloudy days.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: All over the world, incentives designed to decrease the dependence on oil and coal have led to a steep increase in wind-powered energy. Today, Asia leads the world in wind power, producing around 230,000 megawatts,¹ the equivalent of 230 large coal-powered plants. Europe produces nearly 180,000 megawatts. North America remains in a distant third, at 105,000.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Despite its success, some people are protesting wind-power development, saying the turbines² are both noisy and ugly. Just outside England’s Lake District—a protected national park—a dozen existing wind towers are due to be removed. “This is a high-quality landscape,” says one local homeowner. “They shouldn’t be putting those things in here.”

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: There are other challenges, too. If the wind doesn’t blow, the turbines are not able to produce adequate energy. As a result, other power sources are needed. In contrast, a strong wind can create too much power. In cases like this, the energy company must sell the extra power at a much-reduced rate, which is not good for business.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: What’s needed for both wind and solar is a way to store a large energy surplus.³ However, most systems are still decades away from making this a reality. On the plus side, both wind and solar power enable people to generate their own energy where they live: People can have their own windmills or solar panels, with batteries for calm days.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.heading: Nuclear
paragraphs.text: In the 1970s, nuclear power was seen as the main energy alternative. Nuclear power produces vast amounts of electricity more cheaply than gas or coal, with no carbon emissions. For a number of years in the 1980s and ’90s, however, use of nuclear power declined due to accidents, concerns about nuclear waste storage and disposal, and high construction costs.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Today, times are changing. Worldwide, about 450 plants generate 11 percent of the planet’s electric power, and some countries have invested heavily in nuclear energy. France, for instance, gets three-quarters of its electricity from nuclear power, the highest percentage of any country. China has started to build one or two new plants a year, and India has also begun to utilize nuclear energy on a large scale.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: However, there are still concerns about the safety of nuclear power, as seen, for example, at the Fukushima nuclear power plant in Japan. The country had to close the nuclear reactors at Fukushima when the plant was hit by a tsunami and, as a consequence, began releasing substantial amounts of radioactive materials. Many still believe, however, that nuclear power is one of the future’s greenest energy alternatives.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: In the end, are any of these sources alone the answer to our current energy problems? The short answer is no, but used in some combination—along with other power sources—we may find ways to reduce and eventually eliminate our dependence on fossil fuels.

notes: 1. A megawatt is a unit of power.
2. A turbine is a machine that uses water, steam, or wind to turn a wheel to produce electricity.
3. If you have a surplus of something, you have more of it than you need.

image.alt: Wind turbines on snow-covered hills at sunset.

B.label: Reading B
B.title: City of the Future?

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: To appreciate the audacity¹ of Dubai, you could start by going skiing. The ski resort, located inside one of the city’s shopping malls, looks from the outside like a silver spaceship. You put on a thick coat, pull on your gloves—and then marvel at what strong air-conditioning can do. At the exit, you can buy a souvenir T-shirt. A cartoon thermometer in Celsius announces: “I went from +50 to minus 8!”

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Indoor skiing in the desert has become a symbol of Dubai’s status as a wealthy, modern metropolis. Originally a small fishing village, Dubai’s fortunes changed forever with the discovery of oil in the 1960s. Since then, it has evolved to become the largest city in the United Arab Emirates, with over three million residents, huge shopping malls, and a hundred high-rise towers. But the rapid growth has come at a price. To power its cars and air-conditioning, the city has produced large amounts of carbon dioxide (CO₂) from fossil fuels. By 2006, Dubai had one of the largest ecological footprints in the world. But now it is making some big changes.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: To reduce its dependence on cars and lower its emissions, Dubai has invested in solar energy, green buildings, and a comprehensive public transportation system. Gleaming driverless trains now run beside the main roads. In addition, all new buildings must meet strict energy regulations. Smart lighting and cooling systems must switch off when no people are present in a room. New buildings must also use solar panels for water heating. “The leadership has recognized that the growth of the economy is not sustainable without taking action on emissions,” says Tanzeed Alam, a climate and energy specialist.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The most striking development can be found where the city’s suburbs meet the desert. Unlike much of Dubai, the Sustainable City to the south feels more like a close-knit² village community. About five hundred low-rise houses are distributed along attractive, tree-lined streets. They all face north, away from direct sunlight, and are close together to provide natural shade. Each building has reflective³ windows and wall paint, which reduce the heat absorbed from the sun. Rooftop solar panels and energy-saving lights contribute to the community’s energy efficiency. As a result, residents of the Sustainable City now consume 50 percent less energy than people living in other parts of Dubai.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: A decade ago, the idea of a fully sustainable community was thought to be unrealistic. But times have changed, says Faris Saeed, one of the creators of the Sustainable City. So, too, have prices. The cost of living in the Sustainable City is similar to some of Dubai’s other neighborhoods. “It’s a myth⁴ that sustainable has to be more expensive,” Saeed says.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Dubai’s leaders hope the Sustainable City will become a model for the future. By 2050, the government intends to obtain 75 percent of the city’s energy from renewable sources—mainly solar. It also wants to have the smallest ecological footprint in the world. The plan is audacious. But if successful, even guilt-free skiing in the desert could become an environmentally sustainable reality.

paragraphs.heading: Dubai’s Sustainable City
paragraphs.text: Dubai’s Sustainable City generates its own power from solar panels placed beside roads and on rooftops (1). It also recycles all of its waste: The all-organic waste is used in domed greenhouse farms (2) to grow vegetables. No gas-powered cars are allowed; residents travel by electric cars or on electric buses (3).

paragraphs.heading: What Makes a Green Building? — General Design
paragraphs.text: Though standards for green buildings vary, they are generally designed to use less energy and water and improve the indoor environment, including air quality.

paragraphs.heading: Improved Insulation
paragraphs.text: Energy efficiency is increased by reducing the amount of air that escapes.

paragraphs.heading: Building Orientation
paragraphs.text: Positioning a building away from (or toward) the sun impacts heating and cooling.

paragraphs.heading: Rooftop Plantings
paragraphs.text: Small plants on roofs retain rainwater and help keep cities cooler.

paragraphs.heading: Enhanced Ventilation
paragraphs.text: Improving air flow can result in a healthier indoor environment.

paragraphs.heading: Water Conservation
paragraphs.text: Efficient bathrooms—including reusing waste water—reduce consumption.

paragraphs.heading: Motion Detection Sensors Control Light
paragraphs.text: Smart lighting turns off if no one is in the room.

paragraphs.heading: Building Materials
paragraphs.text: Eco-friendly building materials reduce emissions.

paragraphs.heading: Other Features in the General Green-Building Diagram
paragraphs.text:
Solar panels
Indoor lighting adjusts to light levels outside
High-efficiency light fixtures
Smart heating and cooling systems
Rainwater utilization systems

notes: 1. Audacity is a willingness to be bold and daring.
2. A group of people that is close-knit is tightly connected.
3. If a surface is reflective, it casts back light or heat.
4. A myth is a widely held but false belief or idea.

questions.prompt: 1. If you protest an action, you are ____ it.
questions.explanation: “Protest an action” nghĩa là phản đối hành động ấy, nên bạn đứng “against” nó. “For” mang nghĩa ủng hộ và trái với “protest”. Bài dùng từ này khi người dân phản đối phát triển điện gió.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 7A, p. 111 (PDF 109), Vocabulary Practice B1; Teacher’s Book, p. 46, key B1.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence with the correct answer.
questions.prompt: 2. If a country’s energy capacity increases, it ____ more energy.
questions.explanation: “Capacity” là khả năng hoặc năng lực tạo ra năng lượng. Khi năng lực ấy tăng, quốc gia có thể sản xuất nhiều năng lượng hơn (“can produce”), chứ không nhất thiết có nhu cầu nhiều hơn (“needs”).
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 7A, p. 111 (PDF 109), Vocabulary Practice B2; Teacher’s Book, p. 46, key B2.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence with the correct answer.
questions.prompt: 3. Over the last 100 years, ____ has been declining.
questions.explanation: “Declining” nghĩa là giảm hoặc suy giảm. Trong hai lựa chọn của câu, “environmental quality” phù hợp với ý chất lượng môi trường suy giảm; “the world’s population” không phù hợp vì dân số thế giới tăng trong khoảng thời gian được nói đến.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 7A, p. 111 (PDF 109), Vocabulary Practice B3; Teacher’s Book, p. 46, key B3.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence with the correct answer.
questions.prompt: 4. A steep rise in prices takes place over a ____ period of time.
questions.explanation: “A steep rise” là mức tăng mạnh hoặc nhanh, được hình dung bằng đường biểu diễn dốc lên. Vì vậy trong ngữ cảnh này mức tăng xảy ra trong khoảng thời gian ngắn (“short”); “long” không diễn tả tốc độ tăng mạnh mà câu đang kiểm tra.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 7A, p. 111 (PDF 109), Vocabulary Practice B4; Teacher’s Book, p. 46, key B4.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence with the correct answer.
questions.prompt: 5. If you guarantee someone a pay raise, you ____ them more money.
questions.explanation: “Guarantee” nghĩa là bảo đảm hoặc cam kết chắc chắn. Đảm bảo tăng lương cho ai là hứa trả thêm tiền (“promise”), không phải từ chối (“refuse”).
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 7A, p. 111 (PDF 109), Vocabulary Practice B5; Teacher’s Book, p. 46, key B5.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence with the correct answer.
questions.prompt: 6. If you dispose of something, you ____.

questions.source: Student Book, Unit 7A, p. 111 (PDF 109), Vocabulary Practice B6; Teacher’s Book, p. 46, key B6.

A.label: Reading A
A.title: CHINA’S GRAND CANAL

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: For centuries, the power of Chinese emperors rose and fell with their control of the Grand Canal. Today, this waterway is shorter than it once was, but it is still the longest man-made river in the world. Importantly, the Grand Canal continues to provide a vital cultural and economic link for modern China.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.heading: Construction Begins
paragraphs.text: The original canal system began around the year 605. China’s Emperor Yang realized that he needed a better way to feed his army. Specifically, he needed a way to move food quickly from China’s southern rice-growing region to the country’s north. So, the emperor ordered the construction of the first section of the Grand Canal, connecting existing canals, lakes, and rivers. An estimated one million people—mostly farmers—worked on the construction, which took six years.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Over the next 500 years, the canal’s importance grew. However, by 1127, parts had begun to deteriorate.¹ In 1279, Kublai Khan began to repair and build new parts of the canal. This renovation created a more direct north–south route to and from Beijing. Future rulers continued to expand and improve the waterway, and it eventually became a vital national lifeline.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: In addition to moving rice around China, the Grand Canal was an important cultural conduit.² Soldiers, merchants, and artists transported ideas, regional foods, and cultural practices from one part of China to another. According to legend, this is how Beijing acquired two of its best-known trademarks. Peking³ duck, a dish from Shandong Province, and the Peking opera, from Anhui and Hubei regions, were both brought north via the canal.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.heading: The Modern Canal
paragraphs.text: For more than a thousand years, goods have been transported along the Grand Canal. Even today, the country’s watery highway plays an important economic role in China. Boats continue to carry tons of coal, food, and other goods to points between Hangzhou and Jining—now the northernmost city the canal reaches. In addition, local governments—eager to increase tourism and real estate⁴ development—are beautifying areas along the canal.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: This development comes at a price, though. In Yangzhou, the city has torn down almost all of the older canal-side buildings. Farther south in the cities of Zhenjiang, Wuxi, and Hangzhou, the situation is similar. In Hangzhou, for example, almost all of the ancient buildings have been demolished. “Traditionally we talk about 18 main cities on the Grand Canal, and each had something unique and special about it,” explains Zhou Xinhua, the former vice director of the Grand Canal museum in Hangzhou. “But now many of these cities are all the same: a thousand people with one face.”

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: In 2005, a group of citizens proposed that the historic Grand Canal be made a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This status would protect the waterway and the architecture around it. “Every generation wants the next generation to understand it, to look at its monuments,” said Zhu Bingren, an artist who cowrote this proposal. UNESCO status was officially granted in 2014. The hope now is that the Grand Canal—one of the world’s great engineering accomplishments—will continue to link north and south China for centuries to come.

paragraphs.heading: CHINA’S LIFELINE
paragraphs.text: At the height of its golden age (1368–1855), China’s Grand Canal ran 1,770 kilometers from Beijing to Hangzhou and transported everything from food to wood to textiles.

Beginning in 1751, Emperor Qianlong made six inspection tours of the Grand Canal, visiting different ports and cultural sites. By 1855, the Yellow River had changed course, destroying parts of the canal.

notes: 1. If something deteriorates, it gets worse in some way.
2. A conduit is something that connects two or more people, places, or things.
3. Peking is the former name for Beijing.
4. Real estate is property in the form of land and buildings.

image.alt: A stone arch bridge and traditional buildings beside China’s Grand Canal at sunset.

B.label: Reading B
B.title: Highway of Dreams

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A new road that connects the Pacific with the Atlantic could bring riches—and environmental ruin.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Mary Luz Guerra remembers a trip she took in 2003 from the city of Cusco, high in the Peruvian Andes, to her home in Puerto Maldonado, a city in the Amazon rain forest. By plane, this 320-kilometer journey would have taken only 37 minutes, but Mary had traveled by truck along narrow mountain roads, across rushing rivers, and through dense jungle. It took her three days to reach home. During the long trip, she remembers thinking, “I can’t wait till they build that highway!” Almost 10 years after that long journey, Mary’s wish came true.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.heading: Bridging a Continent
paragraphs.text: In early 2012, the Transoceanic Highway opened to public vehicles for the first time. A dream of Peru’s political leaders since the 1950s, work on the vast network of roads and bridges began in 2006 and was completed in 2011. Today, the east–west passageway spans 2,600 kilometers. From Peru’s Pacific Ocean coastline, it continues across the Andes Mountains and through a large part of Peru’s Amazon rain forest. It then travels into Brazil, where it connects with a network of existing highways to the Atlantic.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The Transoceanic Highway has been celebrated as one of South America’s greatest engineering feats, and supporters say it will greatly improve people’s lives. Until recently, travel between the cities of Cusco and Puerto Maldonado in Peru took days by bus or truck—as Mary’s story illustrates—and drivers had to use narrow, partially unpaved¹ mountain roads. Now the trip only takes a few hours, and is much safer.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.heading: Improving People’s Lives
paragraphs.text: In addition to making travel faster and easier, supporters say the highway will be good for business. There is enormous demand in North America and Asia for Brazilian and Peruvian products, including soybeans, beef, and gold. A number of companies in Cusco and Puerto Maldonado also sell wood to different corners of the world. Many of these companies transport their lumber² to the Pacific, where it travels by ship to other countries. Thanks to the highway, wood can now reach the Pacific in days; in the past, it could take a week or more. This lowers costs and allows the wood to reach customers sooner, and in better condition. In the long run, say many business owners, this will mean more profit.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The highway will also open up areas of the Peruvian Amazon that were not accessible just a few years ago. This may increase activity in these areas and give people new places to live in and travel to. This, in turn, could mean more jobs and money for Peruvians.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.heading: Environmental Challenges
paragraphs.text: Despite the highway’s many potential benefits, environmentalists are concerned. The Transoceanic passes directly through a large part of the Amazon rain forest, in the state of Madre de Dios in Peru. According to a Peruvian government study, the forested area in the western mountains of this state has the greatest biodiversity³ of any place on Earth, and until recently, large parts of the forest were in pristine⁴ condition. As more people move into the region, environmentalists worry about the impact this will have on the Amazon’s plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Shortly after the highway opened, large numbers of people began coming into Puerto Maldonado from all over Peru—and the world—to mine gold. There’s a lot of money to be made in mining, as well as in farming, says environmental photographer Gabby Salazar. “I think we’re going to see a big increase in farming,” she says. “Right across the border in Brazil, you see soybean farms all over the place.” Studies show that 95 percent of the deforestation⁵ of the Brazilian Amazon occurs within 50 kilometers of a highway, and environmentalists like Salazar are concerned that the same thing is happening in Peru. “It’s having an impact on the environment,” she explains. “It’s having an impact on the people as well.”

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Faced with these risks, many Peruvians talk about the importance of being practical. “In rural⁶ Peru, a lot of people are living in poverty, so it’s very difficult to say don’t build the highway,” explains Roger Mustalish, president of the Amazon Center for Environmental Education and Research. “But every time you see a road like this going through, you soon see major changes.” Will these changes be mostly positive or negative? Many Peruvians are hopeful, but only time will tell.

image.alt: Map of the Transoceanic Highway through Peru and Brazil, showing Cusco, Puerto Maldonado, Madre de Dios and the Pacific coast; the legend distinguishes the highway from existing roads, with a 200-kilometer scale.

notes: 1. If a road is unpaved, it is mostly dirt.
2. Lumber is wood that has been cut into boards.
3. Biodiversity is the existence of a wide variety of living things (plants, animals, insects, etc.) in a certain place.
4. If something is pristine, it is in its original condition or is unspoiled.
5. Deforestation is the destruction or cutting down of all the trees in an area.
6. Rural places are in the country, far away from cities.

The 77-kilometer Panama Canal is one of the world’s greatest engineering achievements. There were (1) ____ for a canal as early as the 16th century, but it wasn’t until 1881 when the French started to build a canal.

The United States (2) ____ the canal project in the early 20th century for $40 million. Construction was completed in 1914 under the supervision of chief engineer George Washington Goethals. A (3) ____ honoring Goethals stands today in Panama City.

A recent $5.2 billion (4) ____ and expansion project allows much larger ships to pass through the canal. This has led to a sharp increase in the amount of goods that can be (5) ____ through the canal. Today, nearly 14,000 ships pass through the Panama Canal every year.
questions.prompt: 1. There were ____ for a canal as early as the 16th century.
questions.explanation: Câu nói về những kế hoạch hoặc đề xuất xây kênh đã xuất hiện từ thế kỷ XVI, nên dùng “proposals”. “Monuments” là các công trình tưởng niệm, không thể hiện những ý tưởng xây dựng chưa được thực hiện. Dạng số nhiều “proposals” cũng phù hợp với “There were”.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 8A, p. 128 (PDF 126), Vocabulary Practice A1; Teacher’s Book, p. 52, key A1.

questions.source: Student Book, Unit 8A, p. 128 (PDF 126), Vocabulary Practice A2; Teacher’s Book, p. 52, key A2.

questions.explanation: Hàng hóa đi qua kênh được “transported” (vận chuyển), phù hợp với việc tàu lớn hơn có thể đi qua sau khi mở rộng. “Demolished” nghĩa là bị phá hủy hoặc phá dỡ, trái với mục đích vận tải của kênh. Sau “can be” dùng quá khứ phân từ để tạo câu bị động.

questions.source: Student Book, Unit 8A, p. 128 (PDF 126), Vocabulary Practice B3; Teacher’s Book, p. 52, key B3.

questions.source: Student Book, Unit 8A, p. 128 (PDF 126), Vocabulary Practice B4; Teacher’s Book, p. 52, key B4.

questions.prompt: 5. A regional language is spoken by most people in ____ a country.
questions.explanation: “Regional” nghĩa là thuộc một vùng cụ thể, vì thế một ngôn ngữ vùng miền được nói ở “a particular area of” một quốc gia. “All parts of” chỉ toàn bộ đất nước và rộng hơn nghĩa của từ “regional”.

For two decades, engineers worked deep under the Swiss Alps, building a(n) (1) ______ tunnel. When it opened in 2016, the Gotthard Base Tunnel became the world’s longest and deepest railway tunnel. questions.prompt: 1. For two decades, engineers worked deep under the Swiss Alps, building a(n) ______ tunnel.
questions.explanation: “Enormous” nghĩa là rất lớn. Câu tiếp theo cho biết công trình trở thành đường hầm đường sắt dài và sâu nhất thế giới khi mở cửa năm 2016, nên tính từ này phù hợp. “Partial” nghĩa là một phần hoặc chưa hoàn chỉnh, không diễn tả quy mô công trình.
questions.source: Student’s Book, Unit 8B, p. 134, Vocabulary A1; Teacher’s Book pp. 54–55, key and completion notes.

entries.meaning: ảo, được tạo ra hoặc mô phỏng bằng máy tính; virtual reality: thực tế ảo, môi trường mô phỏng cho người dùng cảm giác như đang ở bên trong và tương tác với nó
entries.example: Virtual reality allows athletes to practice in a simulated environment.

entries.meaning: cognition: nhận thức, quá trình tâm trí tiếp nhận và phát triển kiến thức, sự hiểu biết; cognitive: thuộc về nhận thức và các quá trình tư duy
entries.example: The researchers study how physical experience influences cognition.

entries.meaning: thể hiện một ý tưởng hoặc phẩm chất bằng hình thức cụ thể, là hiện thân cho; trong embodied cognition, embodied chỉ sự gắn kết của nhận thức với cơ thể, hành động và trải nghiệm
entries.family: embody (v); embodied là dạng quá khứ/phân từ, dùng như tính từ trong embodied cognition
entries.example: The interview describes embodied cognition as learning through action and experience.

entries.meaning: adopt: tiếp nhận và bắt đầu sử dụng một ý tưởng, phương pháp hoặc công nghệ; apply: áp dụng, đưa vào sử dụng; adopter: người bắt đầu sử dụng một phương pháp hoặc công nghệ
entries.family: adopt (v) ≈ apply (v) trong ngữ cảnh áp dụng; dạng danh từ trong bài: adopters (những người tiếp nhận và sử dụng)
entries.example: Some athletes were early adopters of virtual reality in training.

entries.meaning: conference: hội nghị, hội thảo hoặc cuộc họp để trao đổi và thảo luận; video conferencing: việc tổ chức hoặc tham gia cuộc họp qua kết nối video giữa những người ở các nơi khác nhau
entries.family: conference (n); video conferencing (noun phrase); số nhiều trong bài: conferences
entries.example: Video conferencing allows people in different places to hold a meeting.

entries.meaning: converse: trái ngược hoặc ngược lại; conversely: ngược lại, dùng để giới thiệu tình huống hoặc quan hệ đối lập
entries.example: A larger screen can make details easier to see; conversely, a smaller screen can make them harder to see.

entries.meaning: làm suy thoái, làm hư hại hoặc làm giảm chất lượng; trong bài, gây tổn hại cho lưới thức ăn và hệ sinh thái
entries.family: degrade (v); các dạng trong bài: degrading, degrades
entries.example: Pollution can degrade an ecosystem and disrupt its food web.

entries.meaning: perceive: nhận biết, cảm nhận hoặc hiểu một điều qua giác quan và tâm trí; perception: sự nhận biết, sự cảm nhận hoặc cách nhìn nhận
entries.example: Virtual reality can affect how people perceive information.

entries.meaning: downside: mặt bất lợi; drawback: nhược điểm hoặc hạn chế của một cách làm hay lựa chọn; disadvantage: điểm bất lợi hoặc điểm yếu
entries.family: downside (n) ≈ drawback (n) ≈ disadvantage (n); dạng số nhiều trong bài: downsides
entries.example: One downside of a new technology is that people may use it in harmful ways.

entries.meaning: assess (v): đánh giá; access (v): tiếp cận, sử dụng hoặc truy cập; access (n): khả năng hoặc quyền tiếp cận, sử dụng; trong bài, access to medical supplies là khả năng nhận được vật tư y tế cần thiết
entries.family: assess (v) khác access (v, n); assess something; access something (v); have access to something (n)
entries.example: Drone images help workers assess damage in areas that are difficult to access.

entries.meaning: sufficient: đủ để đáp ứng nhu cầu; adequate: đủ về số lượng hoặc đạt yêu cầu về chất lượng; deficient: thiếu hụt, không đủ hoặc không đạt yêu cầu
entries.family: sufficient (adj) ≈ adequate (adj), trái nghĩa với deficient (adj); deficient in something
entries.example: Clinics need sufficient supplies to provide adequate care.

entries.meaning: poach: săn bắt hoặc đánh bắt trái phép; poacher: người săn bắt hoặc đánh bắt trái phép
entries.family: poach (v) → poacher (n); số nhiều trong bài: poachers
entries.example: The drones help locate poachers who are hiding in the dark.

entries.meaning: thuộc về quân đội hoặc quân sự
entries.family: military (adj), thường đứng trước danh từ
entries.example: A device designed for military use can also support civilian rescue work.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 1. What would be the best alternative title for this passage?

options.label: How VR Brings Us All Together
VR: A Useful Tool for the 21st Century

questions.explanation: Bài phỏng vấn trình bày VR như một công cụ hữu ích cho việc học qua trải nghiệm, luyện tập thể thao, giao tiếp và nâng cao nhận thức môi trường, nên c bao quát nhất. Phương án a thu hẹp nội dung vào việc kết nối con người; b chỉ tập trung vào trò chơi; d chỉ phản ánh ứng dụng môi trường ở Ischia, không bao quát toàn bài.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension A1; paragraph A–K; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key A1.

questions.prompt: 2. Which of these is NOT an example of embodied cognition?

options.label: watching a soccer game on TV
cooking a meal using a recipe

questions.explanation: “Embodied cognition” được giải thích là học bằng cách làm và có trải nghiệm trực tiếp. Xem bóng đá trên TV là hoạt động quan sát thụ động nên không phải ví dụ mà câu hỏi tìm kiếm. Nấu ăn theo công thức, giải ô chữ và chơi nhạc cụ đều đòi hỏi người học thực hiện hoạt động, nên b, c và d phù hợp với ý “learning by doing”.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension A2; paragraph B; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key A2.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 3. What is the purpose of the Ischia VR model?

options.label: to propose a new way of saving sea life near Ischia
to recreate what the climate in Italy was like in the past
to show how oceans are being damaged by climate change
to explain how pollution from Ischia is affecting other areas

questions.explanation: Mô hình Ischia cho người dùng khám phá tác động của CO₂ lên các loài và hình dung đại dương trong khoảng 50 năm tới, nên c diễn đạt đúng mục đích cảnh báo về tổn hại môi trường. Bài không đề xuất một biện pháp cứu sinh vật biển tại Ischia như a; mô hình hướng tới tương lai chứ không tái hiện khí hậu quá khứ như b; và Ischia là nơi được dùng để nghiên cứu, không được nói là nguồn ô nhiễm gây hại cho các vùng khác như d.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension A3; paragraph H–I; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key A3; p. 59, teaching note.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 4. Which of the following is closest in meaning to “adopters”?
questions.explanation: Carson Palmer là một trong những người sớm sử dụng hệ thống VR để luyện tập, nên “adopters” ở đây gần nghĩa với “users”. Anh không được giới thiệu là người phát minh ra hệ thống (b). Dù Palmer là vận động viên và là tiền vệ bóng bầu dục, “athletes” và “quarterbacks” mô tả nghề/vai trò chứ không phải nghĩa của từ “adopters”.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension A4; paragraph D; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key A4; p. 59, teaching note.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 5. What is Bailenson’s main point about VR’s effect on people?

options.label: Although VR technology is improving, other media will still be important.
VR is a major change, but it will not fundamentally change who we are.
It will take several years before people’s lives are really affected by VR.
VR’s impact is significant, but many people in the world will not notice it.

questions.explanation: Bailenson gọi VR là một bước tiến lớn của truyền thông và nói nó tác động khác đến cách tiếp nhận thông tin, nhưng ông không nghĩ nó sẽ thay đổi con người về bản chất. Vì vậy b giữ đúng cả hai ý. Ông không bàn rằng các phương tiện khác vẫn quan trọng như a; không dự đoán phải đợi nhiều năm mới có tác động như c; và không nói nhiều người sẽ không nhận ra ảnh hưởng như d.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension A5; paragraph K; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key A5.

questions.group: B. Write short answers. Use no more than three words from the reading passage for each answer.
questions.prompt: 1. According to Bailenson, how do people learn best?
questions.explanation: Bailenson giải thích “embodied cognition” là “we learn by doing”: học qua việc tự làm, thay vì chỉ quan sát thụ động. Vì vậy “by doing” là đáp án ngắn gọn; “embodied cognition” là thuật ngữ tương đương trong đáp án giáo viên. Các cụm ngắn nói rõ việc học bằng làm hoặc có trải nghiệm cũng diễn đạt đúng ý, trong giới hạn ba từ.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension B1; paragraph B; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B1.

questions.group: B. Write short answers. Use no more than three words from the reading passage for each answer.
questions.prompt: 2. In what other way did VR help American football players, in addition to improving decision-making?
questions.explanation: Bên cạnh tăng độ chính xác khi ra quyết định, nghiên cứu được nêu cho thấy VR giúp giảm thời gian phản ứng. Cụm “reducing reaction times” gồm ba từ và nêu đầy đủ tác động; “reaction times” cũng xác định đúng khía cạnh được cải thiện. Không nhầm với việc học các chiến thuật: đó là cách Palmer luyện tập, không phải tác động thứ hai được liệt kê trong câu nghiên cứu.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension B2; paragraph D; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B2.

questions.group: B. Write short answers. Use no more than three words from the reading passage for each answer.
questions.prompt: 3. In what other way can VR avatars improve video conferencing, in addition to body posture and space?
questions.explanation: Đoạn G cho biết avatar cho phép kiểm soát vị trí cơ thể và giao tiếp bằng mắt theo cách video thông thường không làm được. Vì câu hỏi đã nêu tư thế và không gian cơ thể, phần còn lại là “eye contact”. Cụm “control eye contact” vẫn trong giới hạn ba từ và làm rõ cơ chế kiểm soát này.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension B3; paragraph F–G; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B3.

questions.group: B. Write short answers. Use no more than three words from the reading passage for each answer.
questions.prompt: 4. What does the Ischia VR model allow people to be?
questions.explanation: Đoạn I nói trực tiếp rằng khi dùng mô hình VR, mọi người “get to be scientists”. Họ tự khám phá ảnh hưởng của CO₂ lên các loài trong hệ sinh thái, nên điền “scientists”, không phải chỉ nói chung là khách tham quan hay người chơi.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension B4; paragraph I; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B4.

questions.group: B. Write short answers. Use no more than three words from the reading passage for each answer.
questions.prompt: 5. How is VR similar to other types of media?
questions.explanation: Bailenson mở đầu câu trả lời cuối bằng “VR is a tool, just like any other media.” Điểm giống nhau là VR cũng là một công cụ, nên đáp án giáo viên “it’s a tool” hoặc cụm ngắn “a tool” đều đúng. Đặc điểm dùng cơ thể và tạo cảm giác nhập vai được ông dùng để nói về khác biệt, không phải điểm giống nhau.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 142 (PDF 140), Reading Comprehension B5; paragraph K; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B5.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 1. The downside of something is the ____ aspect of it.
questions.explanation: “Downside” là mặt bất lợi hoặc tiêu cực của một việc, nên chọn “negative”. “Positive” chỉ mặt tích cực và mang nghĩa ngược lại.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 144 (PDF 142), Vocabulary Practice B1; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B1.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 2. At a conference, you are more likely to speak to ____.
questions.explanation: “Conference” là hội nghị/cuộc họp để trao đổi công việc hoặc chuyên môn, nên thường nói chuyện với đồng nghiệp (“colleagues”). Thành viên gia đình (“family members”) phù hợp hơn với các cuộc gặp gia đình, không phải ngữ cảnh đặc trưng của từ này.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 144 (PDF 142), Vocabulary Practice B2; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B2.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 3. If you demonstrate a skill, you ____ it.
questions.explanation: “Demonstrate a skill” nghĩa là thể hiện hoặc làm mẫu một kỹ năng cho người khác thấy, nên “show” đúng. “Hide” là che giấu, trái nghĩa với hành động trình bày hoặc chứng minh.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 144 (PDF 142), Vocabulary Practice B3; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B3.

questions.group: B. Complete each sentence. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 4. You use conversely to indicate an idea is ____ another idea.
questions.explanation: “Conversely” dùng để chuyển sang một ý đối lập hoặc tình huống ngược lại. Do đó ý sau “different from” ý trước, không phải “similar to”. Ví dụ trong bài, nhìn vào camera thì không thấy người kia, còn nhìn vào hình người kia thì không nhìn vào camera.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9A, p. 144 (PDF 142), Vocabulary Practice B4; Teacher’s Book, p. 58, key B4.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 1. What is the reading passage mainly about?

options.label: successes and failures of recent drone technology
how drone delivery times have improved in recent years
examples of positive uses of drone technology around the world
predictions for how drone technology will change in the future

questions.explanation: Bài đọc trình bày các ứng dụng tích cực của thiết bị bay không người lái: chuyển thuốc đến phòng khám xa, khảo sát thiệt hại thiên tai và hỗ trợ bảo tồn động vật. Vì thế c bao quát toàn bài. Bài không cân bằng thành công với thất bại như a; tốc độ giao thuốc ở b chỉ là một ví dụ; các dự đoán ở d chỉ là một phần của nội dung.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 148 (PDF146), Reading Comprehension A1; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A1. Evidence: introduction and paragraphs A–F.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 2. What is the main purpose of Zipline’s drones?

options.label: to transport medicines to people’s homes
to identify clinics most in need of medicine
to deliver medical supplies after a disaster
to get supplies quickly to remote health clinics

questions.explanation: Zipline dùng drone để nhanh chóng đưa vật tư y tế đến các phòng khám ở vùng xa của Rwanda; thời gian vận chuyển giảm từ hàng giờ xuống còn 30 phút. Vì vậy chọn d. Bài không nói giao thuốc đến từng nhà (a) hay dùng drone để chọn phòng khám thiếu thuốc nhất (b). Việc ứng phó thiên tai (c) là ví dụ khác, không phải mục đích chính của Zipline được nêu ở đây.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 148 (PDF146), Reading Comprehension A2; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A2. Evidence: paragraphs A–B.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 3. After the 2015 Vanuatu disaster, what were drones primarily used for?
questions.explanation: Sau cơn bão ở Vanuatu năm 2015, drone chụp ảnh thiệt hại, giúp nhân viên cứu trợ đánh giá tình hình và lập bản đồ khu vực bị ảnh hưởng. Đó là khảo sát thiệt hại do bão, nên a đúng. Bài không nói drone phân tích thời tiết (b), trực tiếp chuyển vật tư y tế (c) hoặc gửi thông điệp khẩn cấp (d) trong ví dụ này.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 148 (PDF146), Reading Comprehension A3; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A3. Evidence: paragraph C.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 4. According to the passage, why are infrared drones especially useful?

options.label: They are silent and difficult to detect.
They can identify poachers at night.
They are cheaper than other types of drones.
They can be used near the ground and in the sky.

questions.explanation: Camera hồng ngoại giúp drone nhận ra người và động vật trong bóng tối, đặc biệt hữu ích vì những kẻ săn trộm thường hoạt động mạnh nhất vào ban đêm. Do đó b đúng. Bài không khẳng định chúng im lặng, khó bị phát hiện (a) hay dùng được ở hai độ cao như d. Mức giá được so với các công cụ công nghệ cao khác, không phải với các loại drone khác như c.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 148 (PDF146), Reading Comprehension A4; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A4. Evidence: paragraph D.

questions.group: A. Choose the best answer for each question.
questions.prompt: 5. Which of these is closest in meaning to “swarms” in “swarms of drones”?
questions.explanation: “Swarms” chỉ những đàn hoặc nhóm rất đông, thường dùng với côn trùng bay. Trong “swarms of drones”, từ này hình dung rất nhiều drone cùng bay trên rừng, nên gần nghĩa nhất với “large numbers”. Nó không nói về loại mới (a), nhóm nhỏ (c) hay nhiều chủng loại khác nhau (d).
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 148 (PDF146), Reading Comprehension A5; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A5. Evidence: paragraph E; Teacher’s Book, p. 61, swarm note.

questions.group:
A. Complete the information. Choose the correct words.

Quadcopters—the most popular type of drone today—work well to deliver (1) ____ and to (2) ____ storm damage. A quadcopter is practical and (3) ____, making it possible for even small organizations to buy. But it’s a noisy machine compared to quieter, but more expensive, plane-like drones.

A(n) (4) ____ new project aims to offer the best of both worlds: ornithopter drones. Ornithopters have flapping wings that can cross the sky quietly and efficiently. They can also take off and land in tight spaces. Drone builders hope to make ornithopter drones that work even more like birds. One day, drones could move as (5) ____ as falcons—diving out of the sky at 320 kilometers per hour.
questions.prompt: 1. Quadcopters work well to deliver ____.
questions.explanation: Sau “deliver” cần danh từ chỉ thứ được vận chuyển. “Packages” là các kiện hàng, phù hợp với công dụng của quadcopter. “Medical” là tính từ nghĩa là thuộc y tế; đứng một mình ở đây không thể làm tân ngữ chỉ hàng được giao.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice A1; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A1.

questions.explanation: “Assess storm damage” nghĩa là đánh giá thiệt hại do bão, phù hợp với việc drone khảo sát và ghi hình. “Aid” nghĩa là giúp đỡ; “aid storm damage” sẽ thành giúp cho thiệt hại và không diễn tả hành động đánh giá.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice A2; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A2.

Quadcopters—the most popular type of drone today—work well to deliver (1) ____ and to (2) ____ storm damage. A quadcopter is practical and (3) ____, making it possible for even small organizations to buy. But it’s a noisy machine compared to quieter, but more expensive, plane-like drones.

questions.prompt: 3. A quadcopter is practical and ____, making it possible for even small organizations to buy.
questions.explanation: Việc ngay cả tổ chức nhỏ cũng có thể mua cho thấy quadcopter có giá phải chăng, tức “affordable”. “Sufficient” nghĩa là đủ về lượng hoặc mức độ, không giải thích trực tiếp khả năng chi trả mà câu đang nói đến.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice A3; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A3.

Quadcopters—the most popular type of drone today—work well to deliver (1) ____ and to (2) ____ storm damage. A quadcopter is practical and (3) ____, making it possible for even small organizations to buy. But it’s a noisy machine compared to quieter, but more expensive, plane-like drones.

One day, drones could move as (5) ____ as falcons—diving out of the sky at 320 kilometers per hour.
questions.prompt: 4. A(n) ____ new project aims to offer the best of both worlds: ornithopter drones.
questions.explanation: Dự án đặt mục tiêu kết hợp ưu điểm của nhiều loại drone và làm máy bay hoạt động giống chim, nên “ambitious” (đầy tham vọng, có mục tiêu lớn) phù hợp. “Rapid” chỉ tốc độ nhanh; câu này mô tả mục tiêu của dự án chứ không cho biết dự án được thực hiện nhanh.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice A4; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A4.

Quadcopters—the most popular type of drone today—work well to deliver (1) ____ and to (2) ____ storm damage. A quadcopter is practical and (3) ____, making it possible for even small organizations to buy. But it’s a noisy machine compared to quieter, but more expensive, plane-like drones.

One day, drones could move as (5) ____ as falcons—diving out of the sky at 320 kilometers per hour.
questions.prompt: 5. One day, drones could move as ____ as falcons—diving out of the sky at 320 kilometers per hour.
questions.explanation: Chi tiết 320 km/giờ nói về tốc độ di chuyển, vì vậy cần “rapidly” (nhanh chóng). Đây là trạng từ bổ nghĩa cho “move” trong cấu trúc so sánh “as rapidly as”. “Ambitiously” nghĩa là một cách đầy tham vọng, không diễn tả tốc độ bay.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice A5; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, A5.

questions.group: B. Complete the definitions. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 1. If you give someone aid, you ____ them.
questions.explanation: “Aid” nghĩa là sự giúp đỡ hoặc hỗ trợ, nên cho ai sự hỗ trợ tức là “help” họ. “Move” nghĩa là di chuyển hoặc làm ai xúc động, không phải nghĩa của “give someone aid” trong định nghĩa này.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice B1; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, B1.

questions.group: B. Complete the definitions. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 2. Someone who is ambitious is determined to ____.
questions.explanation: Một người “ambitious” có tham vọng và quyết tâm thành công, nên chọn “succeed”. Họ có thể muốn giúp người khác, nhưng “help” không phải đặc điểm xác định nghĩa của “ambitious”.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice B2; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, B2.

questions.group: B. Complete the definitions. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 3. If you survey something, you examine it ____.
questions.explanation: “Survey” trong ngữ cảnh này là khảo sát hoặc xem xét kỹ một đối tượng, nên “in detail” nêu đúng mức độ xem xét. Khảo sát không nhất thiết phải diễn ra chậm, vì vậy “slowly” không phải định nghĩa của từ.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice B3; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, B3.

questions.group: B. Complete the definitions. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 4. If something is sufficient, it is ____.
questions.explanation: “Sufficient” nghĩa là đủ để đáp ứng một nhu cầu, tương đương “enough”. “Not enough” là không đủ và có nghĩa ngược lại; vì thế phải chọn phương án b.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice B4; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, B4.

questions.group: B. Complete the definitions. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 5. The military mostly consists of ____ soldiers.
questions.explanation: “The military” là lực lượng quân đội, chủ yếu gồm binh sĩ được trang bị vũ khí (“armed”). “Unarmed” nghĩa là không có vũ khí, trái với định nghĩa khái quát mà câu này kiểm tra.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice B5; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, B5.

questions.group: B. Complete the definitions. Choose the correct option.
questions.prompt: 6. Medical supplies consist of items that improve people’s ____.
questions.explanation: “Medical” liên quan đến y tế, khám chữa bệnh và sức khỏe. Vì vậy vật tư y tế giúp cải thiện “health”. “Wealth” là tài sản hoặc sự giàu có, không phải lĩnh vực mà “medical supplies” trực tiếp hướng đến.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice B6; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, B6.

questions.group: C. The verbs in the options are often used before the noun aid. Choose the correct options.
questions.prompt: 1. Some homeless people ____ aid in the form of temporary shelter.
questions.explanation: Người vô gia cư trong câu là bên nhận chỗ ở tạm thời như một hình thức hỗ trợ, nên chọn “receive aid”. “Provide aid” là cung cấp sự hỗ trợ cho người khác, đảo vai trò người nhận và người cung cấp trong tình huống này.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice C1; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, C1. Teacher’s Book, p. 61, subject note.

questions.group: C. The verbs in the options are often used before the noun aid. Choose the correct options.
questions.prompt: 2. Many college students ____ financial aid to pay for their education.
questions.explanation: Nhiều sinh viên dựa vào hỗ trợ tài chính để trả chi phí học tập, nên dùng “depend on financial aid”. “Withhold” nghĩa là giữ lại hoặc không cấp một khoản hỗ trợ; hành động đó không phù hợp với vai trò sinh viên đang cần tiền để đi học.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice C2; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, C2.

questions.group: C. The verbs in the options are often used before the noun aid. Choose the correct options.
questions.prompt: 3. An aid organization might ____ aid operations if their emergency workers are in danger.
questions.explanation: Nếu nhân viên cứu trợ gặp nguy hiểm, tổ chức có thể tạm ngừng hoạt động để bảo vệ họ, nên chọn “suspend aid operations”. “Call for” nghĩa là kêu gọi hoặc yêu cầu; nó không diễn đạt việc ngừng công việc khi điều kiện mất an toàn.
questions.source: Student Book, Unit 9B, p. 150 (PDF148), Vocabulary Practice C3; Teacher’s Book, p. 60, C3.

questions.group: C. The verbs in the options are often used before the noun aid. Choose the correct options.
questions.prompt: 4. After it was hit by Hurricane Maria, officials in Puerto Rico ____ aid so they could rebuild.
questions.explanation: Sau khi Puerto Rico bị bão Maria tàn phá, các quan chức kêu gọi viện trợ để tái thiết, tức “appealed for aid”. “Extended aid” nghĩa là cung cấp hỗ trợ cho người khác; ở đây họ đang cần nhận sự hỗ trợ để xây dựng lại.

A.label: Reading A
A.title: WHAT’S ON YOUR MIND?

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The ancient Egyptians thought so little of the brain that when a king died, they removed the brain from his body and threw it away. The Egyptians presumed, like many people before and after them, that consciousness—your mind and your thoughts—existed in the heart.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Now we know that the mind is a product of the brain, but how exactly does this 1.5-kilo piece of matter create a mind that allows you to think about yourself, experience happiness and anger, or remember events that happened 20 minutes or 20 years ago? This isn’t a new question. Today, however, powerful new techniques for visualizing the sources of thought, emotion, behavior, and memory are transforming the way we understand the brain and the mind it creates.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Have you ever stopped and thought, “What’s wrong with me today? I just don’t feel like myself”? Perhaps you were more tired or worried than usual—but somehow, you knew that something was different about you. This self-awareness—the ability to think about yourself and how you’re feeling—is an important part of being human.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: This part of your mind has its origins in the prefrontal cortex—a region of your brain just behind your forehead that extends to about your ears. Before this area began to function (around age two), you didn’t understand that you were a separate individual with your own identity. As this part of your brain developed, you became more aware of yourself and your thoughts and feelings. The temporal lobe—a part of the brain associated with perception and speech—helped you understand and put into words these thoughts and feelings.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Perhaps one of the most important factors involved in shaping our identity is memory. What exactly is a memory? Most scientists define it as a stored pattern of connections between neurons¹ in the brain. Every feeling you remember and every thought you think alters the connections within the vast network of brain cells, and memories are reinforced, weakened, or newly formed.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Most people’s earliest memories reach back to about age three or so. Very few people remember anything before this time because the part of the brain that helps form long-term memories (the hippocampus) was not yet fully developed. This doesn’t mean earlier memories don’t exist in your mind, though. Some scientists believe that highly emotional memories, especially those associated with intense fear, might be stored in another structure in the brain (the amygdala) that may be functional at birth. Although these memories are not accessible to the conscious mind, they might still shape the way we feel and behave, even into adulthood.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: But where do our emotions come from, and how do they shape the people we are and the way we perceive the world? Forty years ago, psychologist Paul Ekman demonstrated that facial expressions used to exhibit certain emotions are recognized by people everywhere. Ekman suggested that these emotions and their corresponding facial expressions evolved to help us deal quickly with situations that can affect our welfare.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Though humans may share certain emotions and recognize them in others, we don’t all have the same emotional response to every situation. In fact, most emotional responses are learned and stored in our memories. The smell of freshly cut grass, for example, will generate happy feelings in someone who spent enjoyable childhood summers in the countryside, but not in someone who was forced to work long hours on a farm. Once an emotional association like this is made, it is very difficult to reverse it. “Emotion is the least flexible part of the brain,” says Ekman. But we can learn to control our emotions by becoming consciously aware of their underlying causes and by not reacting automatically to things in our environment.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: But is it really possible to control our emotions? Researcher Richard Davidson has demonstrated that people who experience negative emotions display activity in their right prefrontal cortex. In those with a more positive perspective, the activity occurs in the left prefrontal cortex. Could we, Davidson wondered, control this activity and shift our mental state away from negative feelings and toward a calmer state of mind?

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: To answer this question, Davidson worked with a group of volunteers in the United States. One group received eight weeks of training using different meditation² and relaxation techniques, while another group did not. By the end of the study, those who had meditated accomplished their goal: They showed a clear shift in brain activity toward the left, “happier” frontal cortex.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: For centuries, people have studied the brain, but it is only in recent years that we have really started to learn how it works. Nevertheless, there is still a long way to go before we understand our mind’s many complexities.

notes: 1. A neuron is a cell that is part of the nervous system. Neurons send messages to and from the brain.
2. Meditation is the act of staying silent and calm for a period of time for spiritual reasons, or to relax.

image.alt: A close-up view of branching nerve cells.

B.label: Reading B
B.title: Inside Animal Minds

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: In 1977, Irene Pepperberg, a recent graduate of Harvard University, did something very unusual. Pepperberg was interested in learning if animals could think, and the best way to do this, she reasoned, was to talk to them. To test her theory, she bought an African gray parrot she named Alex and taught him to reproduce the sounds of the English language. “I thought if he learned to communicate, I could ask him questions about how he sees the world,” she explains.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: When Pepperberg began her research with Alex, very few scientists acknowledged that animals were capable of thought. The general belief was that animals reacted to things in their environment but lacked the ability to think or feel. How, then, could a scientist demonstrate that animals might, in fact, possess intelligence? “That’s why I started my studies with Alex,” Pepperberg says.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Certain skills are considered key signs of higher mental abilities: a good memory, an understanding of symbols,¹ self-awareness, understanding of others’ motives, and creativity. Little by little, researchers have documented these abilities in other species. Sheep and elephants can recognize faces. Chimpanzees—who are genetically similar to humans—use a variety of primitive tools for eating, drinking, and hunting; they also laugh when pleased and spit² to show they dislike something. Octopuses in captivity³ are known to amuse themselves by shooting water at laboratory staff. They may even exhibit basic emotions by changing color.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Alex the parrot was a surprisingly good talker. He learned how to use his voice to imitate almost 100 English words, including those for foods, colors, shapes, and numbers. Although imitation was once considered a simple skill, in recent years, scientists have revealed that it’s an extremely difficult ability. Because Alex had mastered many English words, Pepperberg could ask him questions about a bird’s basic understanding of the world. Alex could count, as well as describe shapes, colors, and sizes for Pepperberg; he even had an elementary understanding of the abstract concept of zero.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Many of Alex’s cognitive⁴ skills, such as his ability to understand the concepts of “same” and “different,” are generally attributed only to higher mammals, particularly primates such as humans and apes. But parrots, like great apes (and humans), live a long time in complex societies. And like primates, these birds must monitor the changing relationships within the group. This may explain Alex’s ability to learn a human language. “When we take [parrots] into captivity, what they start to do is treat us as their flock,”⁵ explains Pepperberg. Parrots learn to pronounce and use our words so they can become a part of our group.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Researchers in Germany and Austria have also been studying language ability in dogs. One named Betsy has shown that she is able to learn and remember words as quickly as a two-year-old child. She has a vocabulary of over 340 words, knows at least 15 people by name, and can link photographs with the objects they represent. Like Alex, she’s pretty smart.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: This is the larger lesson of animal cognition research: We are not alone in our ability to invent, communicate, demonstrate emotions, or think about ourselves. Still, humans remain the creative species. No other animal has built cities, created music, or made a computer. In fact, a number of critics dismiss animals’ ability to use tools or understand human language. They believe animals are just copying human behavior.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Yet many researchers say that creativity and language in animals, like other forms of intelligence, have evolved. “People were surprised to discover that chimpanzees make tools,” says Alex Kacelnik, an animal researcher at Oxford University. “But people also thought, ‘Well, they share our ancestry—of course they’re smart.’ Now we’re finding these kinds of behaviors in some species of birds. But we don’t have a recently shared ancestry with birds . . . It means that evolution can invent similar forms of advanced intelligence more than once—that it’s not something reserved only for primates or mammals.”

notes: 1. A symbol is something that stands for or represents something else.
2. If you spit, you force liquid out of your mouth.
3. An animal in captivity lives in a zoo, a cage, or other enclosed place.
4. Examples of cognitive skills include remembering, thinking, and reasoning.
5. A flock of birds is a group of birds.

A.label: Reading A
A.title: VAN GOGH’S WORLD

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Starry nights and sunflowers, self-portraits and café settings—all painted in bold, intense colors. Today, people around the world immediately recognize these as the work of Vincent van Gogh, the Dutch painter. Probably no other artist, at any time in any culture, has achieved such popularity. But who was this man and why, even today, do his art and life have such an ability to move us?

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.heading: An Artist Is Born
paragraphs.text: Vincent van Gogh was born on March 30, 1853, in Zundert, a small village in southern Holland. As a child, he was serious and sensitive. He loved to draw, and his work showed talent, but no one encouraged him to become an artist. Instead, his father thought he should take a “sensible” job—something like a salesclerk or carpenter. As a young adult, he wandered from job to job with little success and very little money, becoming more depressed with each failure. In March 1880, however, just before his 27th birthday, something changed inside van Gogh. He realized that he was meant to be a painter, and he began to study art in Brussels, receiving financial help from his brother Theo.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.heading: Discovering Color
paragraphs.text: In 1886, van Gogh moved to Paris, hoping to learn more about the color techniques being used by Impressionist artists there. Instead of grays and browns, his work began to emphasize blue and red, and then yellow and orange. Soon he began to see life differently: Go slow. Stop thinking. Look around. You’ll see something beautiful if you open yourself. These were the principles that guided his art. With his innovative color combinations, van Gogh wanted to show others how to better appreciate a flower, the night sky, or a person’s face.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.heading: Descent into Madness
paragraphs.text: Few who lived in van Gogh’s time appreciated his work, however. Many laughed when they saw his paintings, which hurt the sensitive artist terribly. In February 1888, he moved away from Paris to Arles, a town in southern France. Often he could not eat or sleep, and stayed up into the early morning hours painting. Days passed, and he spoke to no one. Following an argument with fellow artist Paul Gauguin, van Gogh took a razor and cut off his own earlobe.¹

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: He never explained why he injured himself, but by now, many were convinced that van Gogh was crazy, and, indeed, his mental health started to decline. He began to have attacks during which he would hear strange sounds and think people were trying to hurt him. In the spring of 1889, he was sent to a mental hospital in Saint-Rémy, a town near Arles.

image.alt: Original map showing towns and cities in the Netherlands, Belgium, and France, with no route drawn.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: What exactly was van Gogh suffering from? No one knows for certain, but some now think it may have been a form of manic depression.² Whatever his condition, van Gogh’s illness both inhibited and inspired his creativity. When his attacks came, he could not paint. But during his periods of calm, he was able to complete more than a hundred masterpieces, including the classic The Starry Night. “Working on my pictures,” he wrote, “is almost a necessity for my recovery.”

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Following his release from the hospital in May 1890, van Gogh took a room in Auvers-sur-Oise, a town just north of Paris. For the 70 days that he lived there, he produced, on average, a painting a day. Until his death, however, he was unable to sell a single one; today, those paintings would be worth more than a billion U.S. dollars.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: It was at this time that van Gogh either borrowed or stole a gun. On the afternoon of July 27, 1890, he went out to the country and shot himself in the stomach. Two days later, Vincent van Gogh died at age 37. What caused him to take his own life—his lack of financial success, mental illness, loneliness?

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.heading: Van Gogh’s Legacy³
paragraphs.text: Over a century after his death, van Gogh remains extremely popular. His story—of a man who resisted materialism⁴ and greed, who was alone and unappreciated—gives people something they need. We find pieces of ourselves in him. This may also explain the high prices paid for van Gogh’s work. His Portrait of Dr. Gachet sold in 1990 for more than $80 million to a Japanese businessman, breaking the world record for a painting. Many of his other works have also sold for millions. Of course, people are buying great art when they purchase one of van Gogh’s paintings, but they are also buying a piece of his story, which, like his work, will live on forever.

notes: 1. Your earlobe is the soft part at the bottom of your ear.
2. Manic depression is a medical condition in which one feels alternately excited and depressed.
3. A legacy is something that comes from someone in the past.
4. Materialism is attaching a lot of importance to money and having a lot of things.

B.label: Reading B
B.title: Seeing the Light
B.kicker: In recent years, the artistic achievements of two 20th-century pioneers have been brought to a global audience.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.heading: The Picasso of Brazil
paragraphs.text: In 2018, a major new exhibition opened at New York’s Museum of Modern Art (MoMA). The show brought together more than a hundred works by a single Brazilian artist: Tarsila do Amaral. Although widely celebrated in her native country, the artist was relatively unknown outside Brazil. So who was Tarsila?

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Born in 1886 in a small town near São Paulo, Tarsila do Amaral is considered the mother of modern art in Brazil. She first developed a love for art after her parents sent her to study in Spain. She returned to Europe a few years later, and settled in Paris. Several artists there, including Picasso, were beginning to experiment with new forms—less realistic and more abstract. The new approaches continued to influence Tarsila after she returned to Brazil.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Approaches to art in Brazil at that time were relatively conservative. Traditional European styles dominated, with works mainly featuring natural, religious, or historical scenes in soft colors. Tarsila decided to take a different direction: “I want to be the painter of my country,” she wrote. Her images began to reflect Brazil’s diverse identity—a mix of native, African, and European peoples. She used strong, vivid colors to paint real-life scenes of the nation’s farmers, countryside, and wildlife. This had never been done before in Brazilian art.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: One of Tarsila’s most famous works is Abaporu (1928). The title combines two words from Tupi-Guarani¹ languages, meaning “Man Who Eats People.” The painting has a playful, surreal² quality—but its look and feel are distinctly Brazilian. The work—and its title—later inspired a Brazilian art movement called antropofagia, or cannibalism.³ Brazilian artists began to take in—or “digest”—styles from other cultures and mix them with local influences. The result was something uniquely Brazilian.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Tarsila do Amaral died in São Paulo in 1973, age 86, after a career spanning six decades. But her artwork and legacy live on in her native Brazil. “For Brazilians, her recognition is kind of off the charts,” says James Rondeau, director of the Art Institute of Chicago. “She is the Picasso of Brazil.” Now, with the MoMA exhibition and other international shows, Tarsila’s art is being appreciated by a new audience of admirers around the world.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.heading: The Secret Photographer
paragraphs.text: At first, they seemed like ordinary photographs. A couple holding hands. A child standing by a dirty window. A man daydreaming in a park. The images were hidden in boxes for years, unseen except by the woman who took them: Vivian Maier. But when a collector bought some of these boxes at auction, he soon realized their contents were remarkable. Maier’s street scenes might seem ordinary, but they were actually very special.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Vivian Maier was born in New York City in 1926, the daughter of French and Austrian immigrants. For most of her early life, she moved between New York and Europe. In 1956, she moved to Chicago, where she worked as a nanny⁴ and caregiver. In her free time, she walked the city streets, taking pictures and developing her photography skills. It was a hobby she would continue for the rest of her life.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Maier’s black-and-white images mostly portray urban life: street scenes and regular people. Residents carry out everyday tasks—shopping, riding on buses, walking in a park. Often, she took her pictures in secret. People are caught acting naturally, unaware that they are being photographed. Many of the photos reveal something personal—and often deeply moving. They show us the beauty, humor, pain, and the mystery of normal life.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: In total, Maier took over 100,000 photographs, but she developed very few. Instead, she kept most of the negatives⁵ and a few prints in boxes in a rented storage space in Chicago. Toward the end of her life, she was unable to pay rent to the storage company. So the boxes—with her work inside—were sold at auction.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: In 2007, John Maloof purchased the contents of one of the storage lockers. Realizing the quality of the images, he added a selection of Maier’s photographs to an image-sharing website. Thousands of people worldwide viewed the photos, and many went viral. Maier’s photos began to appear in books and exhibitions. In 2015, a movie about her life—Finding Vivian Maier—was nominated for an Academy Award.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: It is not known why Maier kept her photos secret, or how she might feel about her worldwide fame. She died in April 2009, in a nursing home in the Chicago suburbs. Much of Maier’s life remains a mystery. But her talent as a visual storyteller—for so long hidden in darkness—has finally seen the light of day.

notes: 1. Tupi-Guarani is a group of native American languages spoken in parts of South America.
2. A surreal art style shows objects or a scene in a strange or dreamlike way.
3. In a cultural context, cannibalism is the taking of an idea from one place or context and using it in another.
4. A nanny looks after children in their home while their parents are working.
5. In film photography, negatives are the images used to make print photos.

A.label: Reading A
A.title: DEFYING GRAVITY

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano had a terrifying experience during a spacewalk. While working on the International Space Station (ISS), his helmet¹ began filling with water.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: At first, Parmitano wasn’t sure what it was. “My head is really wet,” he told NASA flight controllers back on Earth. As the water began to accumulate, Parmitano realized there was a problem. “It’s too much . . . Now it’s in my eyes,” he recalls saying. Concerned that he might choke² on the water, ground control stopped the spacewalk. Back inside the ISS, Parmitano took off his helmet and discovered that it contained almost half a liter of water. Where had this water come from?

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: NASA found out that a malfunction³ in the suit’s liquid cooling system had caused water to leak. Some of the water got into Parmitano’s helmet. Though NASA has taken steps to correct the problem, the experience underscores the dangers that astronauts face each time they venture outside a spacecraft.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.heading: Training for a Spacewalk
paragraphs.text: Spacewalks are safer now than they were over 50 years ago, when—in 1965—Russian Alexei Leonov carried out the first one. However, as Parmitano’s experience illustrates, there are still risks involved. To ensure that missions are successful, astronauts train on Earth for hundreds of hours. They learn to deal with the lack of gravity in space, for example, by floating in a large tank⁴ of water, where they experience a feeling very close to the weightlessness of space. For every hour they will walk in space, astronauts practice for 10 hours in the water. They also familiarize themselves with the exact route they will take once they leave a spacecraft. They go over this path repeatedly, so they know exactly what to do on a spacewalk.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Astronauts also train for emergencies that may come about during a walk. One of the most common is losing consciousness. Although spacesuits have an internal heating and cooling system, they can still get very hot, especially when astronauts are doing physically demanding work outside the spacecraft for hours. Astronauts are trained to monitor their breathing and to make sure their bodies aren’t overheating, which could cause them to pass out. Another potential challenge that astronauts are trained to deal with is being separated from a spacecraft. During a walk, astronauts work in pairs and are attached to the ISS for safety reasons. Every NASA spacesuit has a mini jetpack, and astronauts are trained to use it to float back to the station if they somehow become detached from the craft.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.heading: Sunita Williams: Spacewalker
paragraphs.text: As a child, Sunita Williams believed that space travel would be routine when she grew up—something everyone did. She never thought she’d be one of the pioneers. The former pilot has now visited the International Space Station several times, and has spent dozens of hours walking in space.

paragraphs.heading: National Geographic: What’s the most impressive thing about a spacewalk?
paragraphs.text: Sunita Williams: The view—being up very high looking down and seeing the northern lights below.

paragraphs.heading: NG: Is it scary?
paragraphs.text: SW: On my first walk in 2006, there was a problem with a solar array (a solar panel) on the station, and we needed to fix it. A long arm connects the space station to the array. As I started going up this arm to the array, I felt like I was climbing a skyscraper. I had to tell myself, “It’s okay. You’re not going to fall.” In space, you can get really confused sometimes. You don’t know if you are going up or down, left or right. During that first walk outside the ISS, I had to remind myself how we trained in the water tank. That helped me stay calm.

paragraphs.heading: NG: Are there things you do to keep yourself grounded⁵ while living in space?
paragraphs.text: SW: On my first flight, I would go down to the Russian end of the space station because there was only one bathroom at the time. Astronaut Misha Tyurin would always say, “Would you like some tea?” We would sit or float in the air for five or ten minutes drinking tea and just talk about life.

notes: 1. A helmet is a protective hat made of strong material that often covers the face.
2. If you choke on something, you cannot breathe because something is stuck in your throat.
3. A malfunction is a failure to work normally.
4. A tank is a large container that holds liquid (like water) or gas.
5. If you are grounded, you behave in a calm, sensible way, like a normal person.
